text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created: hyperion private VPC — degraded egress/ingress paths (NLB/ALB healthchecks failing). Pager: @vikram oncall
sara: Seeing 502s for Hyperion's /api/generate behind their private NLB. Affected tenant is on our private pool in us-west-2. Customer reports increased latency then errors. :warning:
vikram: I'm on it. Assigning triage. What do we know so far?
mike: ALB healthchecks to backend instances are flapping. NLB target group shows healthy=1/4. Traffic is asymmetrically hitting one AZ.
nancy: DNS for hyperion-private.redwood.internal appears to resolve, but TTL is 300. No recent Route53 changes from our side in the last 2h.
sara: Hypothesis: security-group or route change in the tenant VPC or natgw saturation causing backend failure. Also seeing elevated conntrack counts on VN-hosts.
ops-bot: Alert: conntrack count on hst-priv-natgw-02 = 85% of conntrack-max; dropped packets observed. (metrics link)
vikram: Can someone pull NLB target health and instance logs? I want target headers and 502 traces.
mike: Running: 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:.../tg-hyperion-api
kubectl -n hyperion logs deploy/api --since=10m | tail -n 200
``` 
mike: NLB shows 3 targets Unhealthy with TLS handshake errors, one target Healthy. Backend logs show repeated 503 from upstream connector with `connect: connection reset by peer`.
sara: Check SGs: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0abcd1234` — looking for recent changes.
ops-bot: No SG change events in CloudTrail for that security group in last 24h.
nancy: Customer-side network team confirmed they did a firewall rule tweak 20m ago to block outbound flows to 10.0.0.0/16 for application egress testing. They just DM'd: might be the cause. hyperion-oncall: confirming — we toggled a restrictive egress rule to test isolation, forgot that our private gateway uses that CIDR for inter-AZ health probes.
hyperion-oncall: Sorry, that was us. Rolling back now.
vikram: OK, while rollback happens, we need to avoid customer downtime. Plan A: shift traffic to standby NLB in another subnet/AZ. Plan B: create temporary egress NAT bounce via shared transit for healthchecks.
sara: Can we update routing to redirect healthchecks to healthy AZ? Risky. Prefer using standby NLB if available.
mike: Standby NLB exists but has smaller capacity. We can DR traffic with weights. I'll prepare a weighted DNS change with low TTL.
nancy: DNS-bot, prepare to lower TTL and create weighted record.
dns-bot: Will lower TTL for hyperion-private.redwood.internal to 30s and create weighted record (primary primary/secondary 90/10) when given sign-off.
vikram: Go ahead with TTL change. mike, coordinate the weight shift. sara, confirm rollback from Hyperion.
sara: Hyperion says rollback started at 4280012355 and completed at 4280012360.
hyperion-oncall: Rollback complete. Our firewall rule removed. Monitoring.
ops-bot: conntrack on hst-priv-natgw-02 dropping, but trending down after rollback.
mike: Lowered TTL to 30s (dns-bot). Creating weighted record now: set weight primary->secondary 75/25 to drain.
```
# route53 change batch (abbrev)
ChangeBatch: {"Comment":"HA failover for hyperion", "Changes":[...] }
```
mike: Switching weights now.
nancy: ALB target health recovering: healthy=3/4 -> 4/4 reported at 4280012366.
vikram: Observed 502s drop to baseline, latency back to normal. Hyperion confirm per-app?
hyperion-oncall: We see success on our side, errors gone. Thank you.
sara: Root cause: customer-side firewall egress rule blocked health probe/subnet traffic causing asymmetric NLB health and conntrack spikes on NAT. Mitigation: rollback + short TTL weighted DNS shift while rollback completed.
vikram: Next actions: 
- Document runbook gap: remind customers about blocking egress CIDRs used by healthchecks (link to onboarding doc). 
- Add cross-check in on-boarding: list of probe CIDRs and ports. 
- Consider adding automatic detection: if NLB health drops and conntrack high, alert oncall with recommended checklist.
mike: I'll file infra ticket to add a metric-based runbook suggestion and a small playbook snippet.
nancy: I'll send a quick post-incident note to Hyperion with guidance and ask for scheduled change window for any future egress tests.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (SEV3) — primary mitigations applied; monitor for 1h. Incident owner: @vikram
vikram: Thanks all. If no regressions by +1h, I'll mark done and write short postmortem.
sara: Nice quick rollback by hyperion-oncall and good coordination. :thumbsup:
mike: filing ticket: INFRA-1234
nancy: pinging docs for onboarding update.
vikram: handoff to @mike for follow-ups. I'm back on normal rotation.
mike: taking follow-ups.
nancy: closing communication loop with Hyperion in 30m.
